findings.evidence:
Invariant 2 regex at line 52 of `docs/plans/WP-SCP-024-estate-cascade.md` (991d66c):
```
TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+(?:\*\*)? \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): \S.{19,}
```

Python re.search verification against all 6 worked examples in the plan-doc:
- ✅ `- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): Renovate disabled on PIM; operator-bumped @abc123 at 024C; track until adopter enables Renovate cohort.` → PASS (STATUS.md bullet format with closing `**` — the critical fix target)
- ✅ `See TF-024X-conflict-jrnb2024-pim (pending): adopter has prior policy-check workflow; awaiting rename PR.` → PASS (DISPATCH-NOTE prose without `**` — optional group handles absence)
- ❌ `- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim**` → FAIL (bare-prefix stub)
- ❌ `- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open):` → FAIL (empty description)
- ❌ `- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open):                    ` → FAIL (all-whitespace 20-char description)
- ❌ `- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): short` → FAIL (only 5 chars)

All 6 produce the expected outcome. The `(?:\*\*)?` optional group correctly accepts the trailing closing-bold marker that STATUS.md bullet format produces, while remaining optional for DISPATCH-NOTE prose embeddings. The regex match starts at `TF-024X` (re.search, not re.match) so leading `**` from STATUS.md bold opening is correctly ignored. Additional edge-case verification: `in-progress` status passes (hyphen in parenthetical correctly matched); uppercase slug characters correctly rejected by `[a-z0-9]`; `**` inserted mid-slug correctly rejected.

R7-NEW-CRIT-001 is CLOSED.

findings.title: §5.6 bullet 2 Renovate version-bump criterion is less explicit than §8 bullet 3 regarding operator-bump Threshold A exclusion; closes-marker claim 'phrased identically to §8' is inaccurate
findings.evidence:
**§5.6 bullet 2 (line 191):**
'≥1 SCP minor version-bump cycle (e.g. v1.2.0 → v1.3.0) has propagated cleanly to those adopters via Renovate (proving version-skew tolerance per invariant 8 + T-024-04).'

**§8 bullet 3 (line 245):**
'Each onboarded adopter has survived ≥1 SCP minor version-bump cycle propagated cleanly — **via Renovate** (a Renovate-issued SHA pin bump PR merged + observed clean on default branch). Adopters who satisfied the per-slice bake via an operator-driven bump (R-024-07 fallback) do NOT count toward Threshold A until a real Renovate cycle has also merged + observed clean.'

The explicit exclusion 'Adopters who satisfied the per-slice bake via an operator-driven bump do NOT count toward Threshold A until a real Renovate cycle has also merged + observed clean' is present in §8 but absent from §5.6. An implementor deriving the Threshold A telemetry schema from §5.6 alone would not see this exclusion rule stated explicitly.

**Why not MAJ:** 'via Renovate' is linguistically exclusive of operator-driven SHA pin bumps — operator-driven bumps are by definition not via Renovate. An implementor reading §5.6 who knows the cascade context would understand 'via Renovate' to exclude operator bumps. Additionally: (a) §8 is the authoritative gate, explicitly called out as 'binary pass/fail'; (b) R-024-07 (line 225) contains the operator-bump exclusion in detail; (c) §5.2 line 134 says the operator-bump path TF 'gating Threshold A credit (per R-024-07)'. The exclusion rule is reachable in one hop from any operator-bump discussion in the doc. This is a documentation clarity gap at §5.6, not a specification defect that creates an actionable bypass.

**Additional note:** The closes-marker at §5.6 line 189 says 'phrased identically to §8 to avoid drift' — this claim is imprecise. §5.6 has 5 bullets (one informational) while §8 has 4 mandatory bullets, and §5.6 bullet 2 is less detailed than §8 bullet 3. The claim would be more accurate as 'substantively consistent with §8 mandatory criteria to avoid drift'. This is a bookkeeping precision issue, not a functional defect.

**This finding was not surfaced by R7** (R7-SCAN-2 addressed the 'three-path vs four CI behaviours' cascade-status enumeration sweep; the §5.6/§8 Renovate bullet comparison was not part of that sweep).
findings.recommendation: Optional (does not block fixpoint): Update §5.6 bullet 2 to include the operator-bump exclusion explicitly, matching §8 bullet 3's phrasing: replace '≥1 SCP minor version-bump cycle (e.g. v1.2.0 → v1.3.0) has propagated cleanly to those adopters via Renovate (proving version-skew tolerance per invariant 8 + T-024-04).' with '≥1 SCP minor version-bump cycle (e.g. v1.2.0 → v1.3.0) has propagated cleanly to those adopters via Renovate (proving version-skew tolerance per invariant 8 + T-024-04). Adopters who satisfied the per-slice bake via an operator-driven bump (R-024-07 fallback) do NOT count toward this criterion until a real Renovate cycle has also merged + observed clean.' Update the closes-marker to 'substantively consistent with §8 mandatory criteria to avoid drift' rather than 'phrased identically'. No blocker — fixpoint is not conditioned on MIN resolution.
